official.deadline_note: No central deadline for individual students: participant deadlines are set by the home or Swiss host institution. At institutional level, accreditation and funding applications are submitted annually at the beginning of March (2026 SEMP funding application deadline was 4 March 2026, ECHE accreditation deadline 24 March 2026), and the funding period starts on 1 June. Movetia states the next application deadline is spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+.
official.application_cycle: Current funding period from 1 June 2026 (institutional applications by 4 March 2026); next institutional call spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+
official.status_note: Mobilities under the current 2026 funding period are being implemented by accredited Swiss institutions; Movetia states the next institutional application deadline is spring 2027, likely within Erasmus+ (Switzerland's planned association from 2027), with detailed information to be published in autumn 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Students do not pay study fees abroad and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation; no tuition fees at the (host) institution.
benefits: European mobility incoming: CHF 1,430 to CHF 4,500 depending on duration and country of origin (study mobility)
Worldwide mobility: CHF 1,750 to CHF 5,000 for incoming and outgoing mobility depending on duration
Traineeship grants calculated on a base of CHF 440 per month (European mobility) or CHF 500 per month (worldwide mobility)
European mobility grants include CHF 100 for sustainable mobility, paid out only when travelling to and from the destination by train, bus or car sharing
Special-needs grant of up to CHF 12,000 for people with disabilities or physical, mental or chronic illnesses
No tuition fees at the host institution and recognition of achievements abroad towards the home degree
eligibility: Enrolled at a higher education institution (university, university of applied sciences, university of teacher education) or college of higher education outside Switzerland; students incl. PhD students
Stay lasting between 60 days and 12 months
An interinstitutional agreement between the home institution and the Swiss host institution
Courses or traineeship at the host institution count towards the student's degree (ECTS credits or equivalent)
For traineeships at a Swiss company or NGO, a Swiss higher education institution must still coordinate the application and pay out the grant
requirements: Contact and apply through the International Relations Office of the Swiss host institution, the only party that can receive and pay out the grant
For traineeships: duration of at least 60 days; students are generally responsible for organising the traineeship, accommodation, insurance and any salary themselves
Special-needs grant: applied for directly via the International Relations Office, ideally two months before and in any case before the start of the mobility
documents: Requirement note (Anforderungsprotokoll) for a special-needs grant, prepared with the International Relations Office before departure
selection_criteria: The application process and the selection of participants are handled by the student's home institution, which nominates the student to the Swiss host institution
Each institution has its own participation criteria and procedures; available destinations depend on the institution's partnerships and are subject to a maximum number of students per destination
Awarding of SEMP grants may be subject to internal criteria; some institutions only award SEMP grants for mobilities within Europe
coverage: Financial support for the stay (travelling and accommodation)
No study fees charged at the Swiss host institution
CHF 100 sustainable-mobility contribution included in European mobility grants
Additional special-needs grant of up to CHF 12,000 for costs arising from a disability or physical, mental or chronic illness
For traineeships, insurance and any visa fees are at the participant's expense
application_method: Contact the International Relations Office of the Swiss host institution (for a traineeship at a company or NGO, find a Swiss institution willing to coordinate)
The home institution nominates the student to the Swiss host institution
The Swiss host institution coordinates the SEMP grant application and pays out the grant
official.application_route: Apply through the International Relations Office of the Swiss host institution; the home institution nominates the student and the Swiss host institution coordinates the SEMP application and pays the grant.
official.citizenship_residency: No citizenship restriction published; incoming mobility is open to students of higher education institutions abroad, and worldwide mobility is eligible for funding alongside European mobility.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible: incoming mobility is the route for students from abroad, with European and worldwide mobility grant rates.
official.duration: 2 to 12 months per stay (minimum 60 days); one or two semesters for study mobility; traineeships of at least 60 days
official.description: The Swiss-European Mobility Programme (SEMP) is the higher-education part of the Swiss Programme for Erasmus+ that Switzerland operates as an associated third country. Students from abroad, including PhD students, can spend one or two semesters at a Swiss university or college of higher education, or do a traineeship in Switzerland, while remaining enrolled at their home institution and earning ECTS credits. They do not pay study fees at the host institution and receive financial support for travelling and accommodation; the Swiss host institution coordinates the application and is the only party that can pay out the grant.
official.region: Switzerland (host country); worldwide mobility eligible, European mobility rates for European countries
official.program_type: Government mobility programme (higher education), Swiss solution to Erasmus+ - incoming mobility

applicant_utility.summary: This is an exchange grant, not a degree scholarship: you stay enrolled at your home university and study or train in Switzerland for 60 days to 12 months while your home institution credits the work. Money comes as a Swiss franc grant towards travel and accommodation - CHF 1,430 to 4,500 for European incoming study mobility, CHF 1,750 to 5,000 worldwide, and traineeship grants build on CHF 440 to 500 per month - while study fees at the Swiss host institution are waived. Everything runs through two desks: your home university's mobility office nominates you, and the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office coordinates the SEMP application and pays the grant, so contact both early and confirm the Swiss side actually offers incoming grants.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Students already enrolled at a university or college of higher education abroad who want one or two fee-free semesters, or a 2-12 month traineeship, at a Swiss institution that holds an interinstitutional agreement with their home institution.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your home institution holds an interinstitutional agreement with the Swiss host institution covering your subject and target semester
Contact the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office early to confirm it accepts incoming SEMP applicants and to obtain its internal deadline
Secure your home institution's nomination and a course plan that counts towards your degree (ECTS or equivalent)
Budget the balance yourself: Swiss living costs far exceed the grant, and for traineeships insurance and visa fees are at your own expense
If travelling from Europe, plan train, bus or car-sharing travel so the CHF 100 sustainable-mobility contribution is actually paid out
If you have disability-related needs, raise the special-needs grant with the International Relations Office before departure
common_rejection_risks: Your home institution has no interinstitutional agreement with the chosen Swiss host institution
The Swiss host institution is not SEMP-accredited, does not offer incoming grants, or only funds mobilities within Europe
Missing the host institution's internal deadline or failing to secure home-institution nomination in time
A stay shorter than 60 days, or courses that cannot be credited towards your home degree
A traineeship planned at a Swiss company without any Swiss higher education institution willing to coordinate it
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Swiss accommodation, food, local transport, health insurance (particularly for traineeships), visa fees and personal expenses; the grant only contributes towards travel and accommodation.
document_audit: Grant paperwork is held and finalised by the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office, not by Movetia or the student - send documents there and follow its templates and deadlines
For traineeships you must organise the placement, accommodation and insurance yourself, and any salary is separate from the grant
Special-needs applications need a requirement note prepared together with the International Relations Office before the mobility starts
alerts: Framework change: Movetia states the next call is expected in spring 2027, likely under Erasmus+ following Switzerland's planned association from 2027, with details published in autumn 2026
Institutional funding cycle: applications are made in early March for a funding period starting 1 June, so incoming places depend on the host institution having secured SEMP funding for that cycle
Not all Swiss institutions offer incoming grants - verify support and destinations with the host International Relations Office before committing to course selections
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Home institution nominates the student, the Swiss host institution's International Relations Office coordinates the SEMP application and pays the grant, then a 60-day to 12-month mobility takes place with credits recognised at home.
